content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Fox News's PostFox News Verified accountAugust 23, 2025 · Shared with PublicNew research reveals FTL1 protein drives brain aging by reducing neural connections, slowing metabolism and impairing cognition in the hippocampus of older mice.foxnews.comAging brains could 'become' younger when key protein is decreasedAll reactions:1K375 comments268 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Christopher Shad KenworthyI'm not eating aged mice33w37View all 12 repliesTop fanBob NotilentoLess Protein...more carbs33w8View all 5 repliesHolly HerseyThe article was poorly written so I looked it up. Hope this helps:There are no foods directly containing the FTL1 protein because it is a protein that builds up in the brain, and is associated with aging and memory. You cannot find it in food, but reducing it might help with aging brains and memory, according to Fox News. What is the FTL1 protein? The FTL1 protein is a protein that builds up in the hippocampus, the part of the brain responsible for memory.An increase of this protein is linked to aging and a decline in memory and cognitive function.Can you eat FTL1 protein? No, the FTL1 protein is a specific protein that is not found in food.What can you do to help with FTL1 protein?
